[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is a relaxed recording, we want to capture a short customer story. Quick intros?

For clinical NLP we need consistent 95th percentile under 250 ms for some user-facing flows — we were nowhere near that. Also compliance was front-of-mind, HIPAA stuff, and audits, so we needed better controls.
[01:30] Samir: Yeah and operationally our MLOps team was spending... way too much time on infra fiddly bits. The KV cache yeah, whoever was setting it up would, uh, it would just get cold and we didn't have good shared caching.
[01:44] Priya: (interject) Just to clarify, when you say KV cache you mean pkv cache?
[01:48] Samir: (laughs) I think I butchered it — I meant KV cache.
[01:51] Marcus: That sounds familiar — people mix up cache terms all the time.
[01:55] Sofia: When did you first try Redwood and what was the deciding factor?
[02:03] Dr. Elena: We started a pilot last winter, December 2025, mostly to test latency and cost. The thing that sold us was the Dedicated offering plus the routing/fallback policies — we could pin a smaller quantized variant for certain flows and fall back to the full model if accuracy dipped. Also the observability console — token-level cost breakdowns — that made it easy to justify to finance.
[02:33] Maya: And the onboarding was surprisingly fast, we had a proof of concept in like two weeks, which was key for our product timeline.
[02:40] Sofia: Can you share any numbers on cost or latency impact? If not exact that's okay, ranges help.
[02:48] Samir: Sure. On average per-token inference cost dropped about 40% after we applied batching + prefix caching and moved to Redwood Dedicated. The P95 latency went from ~320 ms to about ~240 ms for our main extraction flow. There's some variance depending on sequence length but that's the ballpark.
[03:12] Marcus: Those are great — do you recall how much caching contributed vs quantization?
[03:18] Samir: Caching was like 18-22% and quantization plus kernel selection the rest; the autoscaler tweaks also reduced tail spikes.
[03:27] Dr. Elena: And importantly the reliability improved. Before we had hours-long incidents where throughput dropped; with Dedicated we hit our SLA targets almost consistently.
